commit.message:
fix(ios-camera): restart audio capture session around AVAudioSession reconfigure (#4285)

* fix(ios-camera): restart audio capture session around AVAudioSession reconfigure

When returning to the app after another app (Spotify, phone call, Siri) reset
the shared AVAudioSession to .playback, the camera detected the category drift
and called configureAudioSessionForRecording(). Its setActive(false)/setActive(true)
cycle, however, runs while the audio AVCaptureSession is still running — which
keeps the now-stale audio route attached and continues delivering buffers
containing only digital silence, producing a recording with a valid AAC track
but no sound.

Stop audioCaptureSession before the setActive cycle and restart it afterwards
so it reacquires a fresh audio route. Also reactivate the session on the
"category already correct" path to recover from interruptions that only
deactivated us without changing category.

* fix(camera): improve audio session handling during interruptions and enhance mic quality

* fix(ios-camera): address review comments on audio session reconfigure

- Synchronize audioInterrupted with NSLock so cross-queue reads from
  videoOutputQueue (captureOutput, startRecording) are no longer racing
  writes from sessionQueue (interruption handler).
- Propagate configureAudioSessionForRecording() failure on the cold
  path of attachAudioToSessionIfNeeded() so audioReady stays honest
  when category/activation fails before the dedicated audio capture
  session is built.
- Restart the dedicated audio capture session whenever it is not
  running after a successful reconfigure, not only when it happened
  to be running before stopRunning() — covers the case where an
  interruption already stopped it before we entered the branch.
- Align DivineCameraPlugin.preWarmFrameworks() with the recording
  path by pre-warming AVAudioSession in .videoRecording mode instead
  of .default, so the warmed audio-session behaviour matches what
  the real recording actually uses.

* fix(ios-camera): only clear audioInterrupted after successful recovery

If attachAudioToSessionIfNeeded() fails after an interruption, captureOutput
must not resume appending audio buffers from a still-broken session — that
would re-introduce the silent-AAC-track failure this PR eliminates. Keep
the flag set on failure so the recording continues without audio.

Addresses review comment by NotThatKindOfDrLiz on PR #4285.

commit.message:
refactor(notifications): delete legacy Riverpod stack (#3596) (#4288)

* docs(notifications): add brainstorm for #3596 deletion

Captures the scope and sequencing reasoning for removing the legacy
Riverpod notification stack (relay_notifications_provider.dart +
notification_model_converter.dart) now that PR #4247 (BLoC migration),
PR #4271 (typed exceptions), PR #4276 (event-driven refresh), and
PR #4277 (dead screen + widget deletion) have all landed.

The only remaining production consumer is
notification_settings_screen.dart's _markAllAsRead, which migrates to
NotificationRepository.markAllAsRead() in the next commits. The
brainstorm documents the snackbar UX, ARB key choice, test fixture
pattern, and the intentional behaviour delta (legacy silently
swallowed server errors; the new repository rolls back and rethrows).

Refs #3596

* feat(l10n): add notificationSettingsMarkAllAsReadFailed

New ARB key for the failure-path snackbar that the upcoming settings-
screen migration will surface when NotificationRepository.markAllAsRead
rethrows after a server failure. The legacy provider silently swallowed
those errors and always showed a green success snackbar.

Style matches the existing failure keys (relaySettingsFailedToAddRelay,
relaySettingsFailedToRemoveRelay) — short, no placeholder, since the
server-side cause is not actionable to the user.

Other locales fall back to English automatically until they are
translated.

Refs #3596

* refactor(notifications): migrate settings screen to NotificationRepository

Last legacy production consumer migrates off relayNotificationsProvider:

- Settings screen's mark-all-as-read now calls
  NotificationRepository.markAllAsRead() through
  notificationRepositoryProvider. The repository's rollback+rethrow
  semantics (PR #4034 → PR #4247) replace the legacy provider's
  silent-swallow behaviour — failures now surface as a red
  VineTheme.error snackbar with the new
  notificationSettingsMarkAllAsReadFailed copy.
- Action card's onTap is null while notificationRepositoryProvider is
  null during early auth, using Material's built-in disabled affordance
  on the ListTile.

Also refreshes the doc comment in notification_realtime_bridge.dart's
_contentForType that pointed at notification_model_converter.dart —
the converter file is deleted in the next commit. The metadata-key
mirroring it described still happens on the REST path inside
NotificationRepository, so the fallback semantics this method relies
on are unchanged.

Refs #3596

* test(notifications): cover settings-screen mark-all-as-read paths

Covers the three observable outcomes of the migrated _markAllAsRead:
green VineTheme.vineGreen snackbar on success, red VineTheme.error
snackbar with notificationSettingsMarkAllAsReadFailed on a server
throw, and disabled ListTile.onTap when notificationRepositoryProvider
returns null during early auth.

The _MockNotificationRepository pattern mirrors the four existing
in-tree uses (NotificationBadgeCubit, InboxNotificationsPage,
NotificationsPage, NotificationRealtimeBridge tests). Only
markAllAsRead is stubbed because the screen doesn't subscribe to the
repository's streams.

Refs #3596

* refactor(notifications): delete legacy Riverpod notifications stack

Closes the dual-notification-system retirement (#3596). The new
BLoC-based lib/notifications/ feature is now the only path; this
removes the legacy Riverpod stack that has had zero production
consumers since the previous commit migrated
notification_settings_screen.dart off it.

Deleted production code:
- lib/providers/relay_notifications_provider.dart (1,092 lines) —
  the RelayNotifications notifier, its NotificationFeedState model,
  the relayNotificationApiService provider, the unread-count provider,
  the loading provider, and the by-type filter provider.
- lib/providers/relay_notifications_provider.g.dart (439 lines) —
  generated companion.
- lib/services/notification_model_converter.dart (224 lines) —
  RelayNotification → NotificationModel converter. Used only by the
  deleted provider; the equivalent enrichment on the new BLoC path
  lives inside NotificationRepository._enrichAndGroup.

Deleted tests (3,295 lines):
- test/providers/relay_notifications_provider_test.dart
- test/providers/relay_notifications_insert_test.dart
- test/providers/relay_notification_api_service_provider_test.dart
- test/providers/relay_notifications_refresh_triggers_test.dart
  (added by PR #4276; its event-driven Site B refresh triggers are
  inherently gone with the file).
- test/services/notification_model_converter_test.dart

Coverage parity: every scenario asserted by the deleted tests has an
equivalent in packages/notification_repository/test/ (refresh +
mark-all-as-read + rollback + acceptRealtime) and test/notifications/
(BLoC + bridge + view). No net coverage loss.

Net change with the preceding 4 commits: ≈ -4,900 LOC.

Closes #3596. Advances #4208 (parent: remove dual notification
system and finish bloc cleanup).

* test(notifications): override notificationRepositoryProvider in scaffold tests

The settings screen now watches notificationRepositoryProvider to disable
"mark all as read" when deps aren't ready. The provider chain requires
auth state plumbing, which the scaffold-structure tests don't mock — they
only verify AppBar/Scaffold colors. Override the provider with null so
the screen renders in its "deps not ready" branch.

* l10n(notifications): translate notificationSettingsMarkAllAsReadFailed

Added in the prior commit to app_en.arb but not propagated to the 16
other locales, which broke the ARB consistency test. Translate the
"Failed to mark all as read" snackbar string for every locale and
regenerate the l10n bindings.

commit.message:
fix(notifications): complete tap-target routing for all notification kinds (#4289)

* fix(notifications): complete tap-target routing for likes, comments, replies, reposts, and mentions

- likes: open correct video with autoOpenComments:false (stable addressable id
  preferred; raw eventId fallback)
- comments/replies: already routed correctly; now fully test-backed
- reposts: open correct video with autoOpenComments:false; actor identity
  verified in test
- mentions: route to root video via NotificationTargetResolver using
  sourceEventId; fall back to actor profile when resolver cannot find a
  video context (plain mentions with no video)
- follow: route to actor profile; now test-backed

Repository changes:
- _mapActorAnchored and enrichOne: extend targetEventId population to
  include mention (uses sourceEventId — the kind-1 mention event the
  resolver walks) alongside the existing likeComment/reply path

View changes:
- _onItemTap: move mention from the profile-navigation branch into the
  resolver branch alongside likeComment/reply
- _navigateToVideo: add mention to isComment check (autoOpenComments:true);
  add profileFallbackPubkey param so mentions with no resolvable video
  context navigate to profile instead of showing a not-found snackbar

Tests:
- Repository: mention carries sourceEventId as targetEventId
- View: like tap (addressable id + raw eventId fallback), repost tap
  (with actor identity), follow tap (profile navigation), mention tap
  (resolver path + profile fallback + null targetEventId fallback)

Closes #4205

* fix(notifications): fix 'video not found' for likeComment by using stable addressable ID

Root cause: likeComment tap resolved the comment event from the relay
and walked its E-tags to find the root video. If the relay didn't
return the comment event or the event lacked proper NIP-22 tags, the
resolver returned null -> 'video not found' snackbar.

Fix: the server already sends referenced_d_tag for likeComment. Combine
it with the user's pubkey to build the stable NIP-33 addressable ID
(34236:pubkey:d-tag) — exactly the same path that makes 'like' taps
reliable. When videoAddressableId is set the tap handler skips the
resolver entirely and navigates directly.

Changes:
- ActorNotification: add nullable videoAddressableId field (constructor,
  copyWith, props)
- Repository (_mapActorAnchored + enrichOne): populate videoAddressableId
  from referencedDTag for likeComment and reply — same pattern as
  _groupVideoAnchored for likes
- View (_onItemTap): destructure videoAddressableId from ActorNotification
  and forward it to _navigateToVideo so the stable path is taken
- Resolver fallback preserved when referencedDTag is absent

Tests:
- ActorNotification: videoAddressableId structure, equality, copyWith
- Repository (batch + enrichOne): likeComment carries videoAddressableId
  when d-tag is present; null when absent
- View: likeComment tap uses addressable ID directly — verifyNever on
  fetchEventById confirms resolver is not called

* fix(notifications): navigate immediately on tap — fetch video concurrently

Before: tap blocked on fetchVideoWithStatsForRouteId (network) before
navigating, causing a visible delay on every notification tap.

After: navigate immediately once the route ID is known. The screen opens
at once showing BrandedLoadingIndicator while the video fetch resolves
in the background via Stream.fromFuture. If the video is null, hidden,
or errors, the route is popped and a snackbar shown on the notifications
scaffold.

The resolver step (relay round-trip for comment/mention taps without an
addressable ID) still runs before navigation — it is required to know
which route to open. All stable-ID paths (like, repost, likeComment with
d-tag) navigate with zero awaits before context.push.

* style: dart format changed files

* fix(notifications): address review feedback

Three issues raised in review:

1. Pop-wrong-route: removed router.pop() from the video fetch callback.

commit.message:
fix(notifications): dedupe WS-first notifications against later REST loads (#4281)

* fix(notifications): dedupe WS-first notifications against later REST loads

Closes the symmetric gap left by PR #4247: a WS arrival followed by a
later REST pagination page containing the same Nostr event no longer
duplicates the row (or the grouped contribution).

Declare a typed `sourceEventIds: List<String>` on `NotificationItem` so
cross-path identity is an explicit, testable contract rather than
repository-private state. `_emitSnapshotForPage` for non-first pages
now uses three gates: (1) `(videoEventId, type)` overlap merges richer
REST groups into existing WS rows in place; (2) `sourceEventIds`
overlap skips cross-path duplicates; (3) `id` equality remains as a
defensive fallback for items with empty `sourceEventIds`. PR #4247's
REST→WS guard (`_knownSourceEventIds` + acceptRealtime early return)
stays untouched.

* fix(notifications): timestamp-driven commentText merge + drop brainstorm doc

Addresses PR #4281 review:

1. `_mergeAppendedVideoGroup` picked `incoming.commentText` first, which
   replaced the newer WS-displayed comment with an older REST-paged one
   (REST pagination walks backward in time). Selection is now driven by
   the side with the larger `timestamp` — mirrors `_groupVideoAnchored`'s
   sort-desc + group.first newest-wins and the surrounding
   `timestamp = max(...)` rule. Falls back to the other side when the
   newer side has no text.
2. Two new regression tests under `group('WS-first dedupe in page-merge
   (#4264)')` lock the rule from both directions (WS-newer-than-REST
   and the symmetric REST-newer-than-WS).
3. Removes the brainstorm md file; its substantive "deferred dedupe
   cleanup" item is now tracked in #4284 and linked from the PR body.

* fix(notifications): align ws/rest dedupe with current main

* fix(notifications): recheck snapshot after realtime enrichment

* test(feed): dispose provider container in feed video tests

---------

Co-authored-by: Liz Sweigart <127434495+NotThatKindOfDrLiz@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
fix(profile): pre-seed cached profile in subscription (#4282)

* fix(profile): pre-seed cached profile in subscription to prevent display name flash

MyProfileSubscriptionRequested was emitting MyProfileLoading(profile: null)
before the Drift watch stream fired its first event. This caused the profile
header to briefly fall back to UserName.fromPubKey, which renders the
generated name (e.g. 'Feminist Sloth 82') while AsyncLoading, before
switching to the real name once the stream arrived.

Fix mirrors the existing pattern in _onLoadRequested: call getCachedProfile
first and carry it in the initial MyProfileLoading emit so the real display
name is shown from frame one.

Closes #4181

* chore(profile): generalize subscription fallback comment

(route now mounts NotificationsPage; inbox tab mounts
InboxNotificationsPage). #4247 explicitly deferred the file
deletion to #4208; doing it here narrowly so #4208's eventual
cleanup is smaller and so AC #2 of #3567 ("no call site
references the legacy NotificationListItem widget") is
satisfied — this screen was that widget's only call site.

The three screen-level test files exercised scenarios already
covered by test/notifications/view/notifications_view_test.dart
and test/notifications/view/inbox_notifications_page_test.dart,
so they are deleted rather than migrated.

The four router/inbox test files that still reference

snapshot; repaired in the next commits.

* test(router): point route_coverage_test at NotificationsPage

NotificationsScreen was deleted in the previous commit. The
BLoC NotificationsPage exposes identical static routeName /
path / pathWithIndex / pathForIndex(int?) accessors, so the
RouteType.notifications parse assertion still holds with a
class-name-only swap.

Refs #3567

NotificationsScreen was deleted; the BLoC NotificationsPage exposes
identical static path accessors. These three test files have
`skip: true` so the tests do not run, but the imports must resolve
for the files to compile under `flutter analyze`.

Refs #3567

* test(inbox): refresh stale doc comment after legacy-screen delete

This comment was already stale post-#4247 (the inbox's default tab
mounts InboxNotificationsPage, not the legacy NotificationsScreen).
Now that the legacy screen is deleted, refresh the comment.

The _MockRelayNotifications mock and the relayNotificationsProvider
override below are intentionally left alone — the legacy provider
they mock still exists for notification_settings_screen, and the
stale-but-harmless plumbing will be cleaned up by #4208.

Refs #3567

* docs(notifications): drop stale 'replaces NotificationsScreen' ABOUTME

The class it was contrasted with no longer exists.

Refs #3567

* test(notifications): cover invite banner show/hide in InboxNotificationsPage

Restores coverage that the deleted notifications_screen_test.dart
asserted (legacy lines 371-426) before #3567 removed the legacy
screen. Three scenarios on the BLoC inbox page's _InvitesBanner:

- Renders _InviteNotificationCard with the plural label when
  InviteStatusCubit reports remaining > 1.
- Renders the singular label when exactly one invite is left.
- Hides the card entirely when no invites are available.

The legacy test's fourth scenario — pull-to-refresh also reloads
invite status — does not apply here. That behaviour was on the
legacy screen's onRefresh and was not ported to NotificationsView
in PR #4247; it's pre-existing #4247-era debt, not introduced by
this PR.

Refs #3567
